reason: Refuted on measurement and on mechanism. (1) The central claim - that the owner's words 'shrink at the exact moment they are being written, then grow back on commit', and that 'the owner cannot see where their title will actually break' - is factually false. render-b.js:732 binds an `input` handler that calls setTitle() on every keystroke; setTitle (render-b.js:632-648) rewrites .b-title and calls C.settle(), which re-runs the word-safe trim. Driven at 1440: with the editor open in the 344px rail (x=186), the row sits beside it at x=710 w=544 and repaints the full string live at 24px/600/28.8px/-0.72px while typing. Screenshotted. At 390 the same typing produced a live-trimmed row ('...before the...') above the sheet (row y=94, sheet y=275, both visible). The specimen the finding says is missing is on screen, in the real typography, at the real measure, per keystroke. The field is the control; the row is the proof - and it is live. (2) The measurement is wrong at the flagship width. At 390 .b-title computes to 17px/-0.255px - identical size and tracking to #b-edit-title. The seven-point gap exists only at >=701px. The finding's own 390 fix (font-size:var(--size-lead)) is a no-op on size. (3) The fix is internally inconsistent and wrong on weight. --size-date is 20px, not the row's 24px, so it would not match even the row it was measured from. Worse, .b-title is weight 400 by default; 600 fires only on data-lead and data-anchor (b.css:263-264). The finding measured the lead row. Five of the seven rows render 400 - measured row1 at 1440: 24px/400. A field hardcoded to 600 would be bolder than the row it edits on the majority of moments, trading one mismatch for a worse one, because the row's weight is semantic and the field is one static control. (4) The fix makes the stated problem worse. #b-edit-title is a single-line <input> (310px, 286px inner at 1440); text scrolls horizontally and can never wrap, so it cannot show a break at any size. Simulated: raising to 24px/600 shows fewer characters before the value scrolls out, so the owner sees LESS of what they typed in the field, while gaining nothing about the break - which is already answered by the live row. It also grows the field 42px -> 47px against a 40px min-height reserve. (5) The lessons rule is misapplied. 'A person's words outrank the machine's... wherever user content appears beside metadata' is a display-hierarchy rule, and it is honoured twice over: 24px title over 11px mono date on the row, and 17px value under an 11px mono 'WHAT IT IS' label in the panel. It does not say a text input must equal the headline it feeds. Making a form control carry headline weight and -0.03em head tracking is the field pretending to be the artefact; Linear, Stripe and Vercel all set editable single-line fields at control size beside a larger live specimen for exactly this reason.
